items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish. Chars voices two funny cartoon characters (a smug gold bar and a nervous banknote), short and punchy, performed exactly as described in each bracket.
lines: Narrator
A four-tonne coin sank to the bottom of the sea, and people kept spending it. Would you accept it?
Narrator
This is Yap, in the Pacific. Its money: rai, huge carved stone discs.
Narrator
The biggest is three point six meters wide.
Chars
[nervous, squeaky banknote, trembling] Imagine breaking that for change.
Narrator
So how do you pay with a coin you can't lift?
Narrator
You don't move it. Everyone just agrees who owns it now.
Narrator
They were cut on Palau, four hundred kilometres away, and carried home by sea.
Narrator
And one stone never made it home.
Narrator
It sank on the way. The islanders agreed it still existed, and kept trading it.
Narrator
That's the mirage: money was never the stone. It was the story everyone believed.
Narrator
Today, your money is mostly numbers in a computer.
Chars
[smug, deep, rich gold bar, very pleased with himself] Speak for yourself. I'm real.
Narrator
So is your money in your account? Or in everyone's agreement?
Narrator
Comment: would you accept a sunken coin?
Narrator
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
